text:
maya: Heads-up — multiple support tickets from EU customers reporting p99 spikes on /v1/generate (~09:10 UTC). Tickets show timeouts and 504s. Any active deploys in eu-west-1?

sam: I see the anomaly on dashboards, p95 jumped from 120ms -> 450ms; p99 ~ 2.1s for last 20m. No infra deploys in the last hour.

ops-bot: ALERT: eu-west-1 serving cluster 7 CPU steal high, queue depth > 85% for model redwood-large-q8 (rollup).

aj: Looking at per-model heatmap — redwood-large-q8 has a hot shard (node-7) with KV cache miss rate up. There are also increased prefix lengths from one tenant (heavy multi-turn chat).

linda: Support says Customer X is sending long contexts (6k tokens) and hitting lots of rerun attempts. Might explain KV pressure.

maya: Ok mitigation plan suggestion: (1) rapidly enable model-fallback routing for high-latency requests to redwood-medium-q4, (2) flip circuit-breaker to short-circuit heavy users, (3) temporary region-fallback to eu-central-1 for priority traffic.

sam: I can flip CB thresholds and enable fallback routing. Propose sequence: A) reduce max_concurrency on node pool for large model to lower queuing, B) enable model-fallback for incoming route, C) lift rate-limits for critical customer if they need it.

aj: Agreed. Quick commands:

```
# enable fallback routing for route id `prod-generate-eu`
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/routes/prod-generate-eu/enable-fallback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"fallback_model":"redwood-medium-q4","max_failures":3}'
# set circuit breaker to 75% util
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/slo/circuit-breakers" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","route":"/v1/generate","util_threshold":0.75}'
```

linda: I'll coordinate support messaging to customers and ask them to reduce context size temporarily. Send a note to Customer X: ask to truncate history to last 3 turns.

maya: Sam, can you also enable short-term KV-cache warming for the large model to reduce miss rate? Maybe prefetch the common prefixes we saw in logs.

sam: Starting with quick mitigations now: reducing concurrency on large-pool, enabling fallback routing, toggling CB. Will post status.

ops-bot: DEPLOY: route change request accepted, job 67234 queued.

sam: Done steps A/B. Concurrency reduced on large-pool: `kubectl scale --replicas=4 dp/large-pool` -> reduces queue depth but may lower throughput. Fallback routing toggled. Circuit breaker set to 0.75 util.

aj: Observability update: within 90s p95 back to ~180ms, p99 down to ~820ms. KV miss rate dropped 12% after prefetch job started.

linda: Support update sent to Customers A/B/C. Customer X acknowledged and will trim contexts.

maya: Good. Next actions: 1) investigate root cause of KV thrashing on node-7 (disk? memory pressure?), 2) add a permanent routing rule to prefer warm replicas for long-context sessions, 3) add a guardrail that auto-falls back to medium model when avg_seq_len > 2048 for non-enterprise customers.

sam: Assigning follow-ups: aj to investigate node-7 (logs, dmesg, kernel OOM?), me to propose permanent CB and fallback policy config, maya to draft post-incident support FAQ and update runbook.

aj: Quick repro steps for debugging (useful for oncall):

```
# synthetic load reproducer (runs many long-context requests)
python tools/repro_load.py --region eu-west-1 --model redwood-large-q8 --parallel 100 --context-file samples/6k_context.json
```

aj: Check these logs: `/var/log/serving/node-7/kvcache.log` and `observability.corp/redwood/trace?span=serve&node=node-7`

maya: tl;dr for pager: mitigation applied — fallback + CB + lower concurrency; metrics improving. Root-cause unknown; suspected KV cache eviction pattern with long contexts. If metrics re-regress, escalate to eng-runtime.

linda: Thanks all — I'll keep customers in the loop. Marking incident as "mitigated" for now. :white_check_mark: 

sam: Leaving notes in the runbook and will schedule a follow-up postmortem tomorrow 11:00 UTC.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated at 09:24 UTC. Actions recorded -> job 67234, ticket 99321.
